title: TypeScript SDK: multiplexed streaming with graceful resume across AsyncIterator & Web Streams
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Teams building real-time UIs and inference pipelines need the TypeScript SDK stream surfaces to support multiple concurrent consumers on the same server stream (e.g., a UI live tail + a background transcript writer) while preserving correct backpressure semantics, deterministic ordering, and the ability to resume after transient network interruptions or token refreshes. Current examples focus on single consumer patterns (AsyncIterator or Web Stream) which forces app authors to duplicate or fan-out streams in application code and handle resume complexity themselves.

Proposal summary:
Implement a lightweight multiplexing layer in the TS SDK that exposes a single canonical source of truth from the runtime response stream and provides: (1) zero-copy multicast to N consumers (AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumers), (2) per-consumer backpressure propagation to the SDK runtime where feasible, (3) resume semantics that allow new consumers to attach mid-stream and historical replays for a short window via in-memory prefix cache, and (4) graceful resume/reconnect when the underlying network or auth token is refreshed. The API should be ergonomic and composable with existing stream helpers (for-await-of, web stream pipes, TransformStreams).

Non-goals:
- Long-term persistent replay store (outside short in-memory window)
- Re-architecting runtime transport (this is an SDK-side feature that uses existing runtime reconnect hooks)

Relevant constraints and trade-offs:
- Memory: in-memory prefix cache must be bounded; choose conservative default (256KB or N messages) with config override.
- Latency: additional multiplexing should not add per-token latency for single-consumer fast paths. Multi-consumer mode may buffer minimally to maintain ordering across consumers.
- Backpressure fidelity: where platform transport cannot convert backpressure signals (e.g., server-sent events), we emulate via consumer soft-flow-control and drop or pause policies documented for apps.

Implementation outline:
1) Add a StreamsMultiplexer class that wraps the low-level stream source. Internally it maintains a ring-buffer prefix cache, a single read loop, and a consumer registry.
2) Expose API helpers: .asAsyncIterator(), .asWebReadableStream(), and .subscribe(callback) for push-style consumers.
3) Backpressure handling: each consumer exposes a per-consumer buffer limit; the multiplexer pauses the upstream pulls when aggregate pending bytes exceed configurable threshold.
4) Resume logic: on transient disconnect the multiplexer attempts automatic reconnect via existing SDK transport hooks and replays from prefix cache. If reconnect succeeds and a token mismatch requires a fresh handshake, multiplexer emits a boundary event so downstream can decide to rehydrate state.
5) Edge cases: consumers that fall behind will receive a "replay_gap" event if prefix window is exceeded. The default behavior is to drop oldest cached tokens and notify the consumer. Configurable to throw/close instead.
acceptance_criteria: New StreamsMultiplexer is exported from ts-sdk public surface under streams.Multiplexer
for-await-of on multiplexer.asAsyncIterator() produces identical token sequence to single-consumer baseline within 1% perf regression for single consumer
ReadableStream returned by .asWebReadableStream() is pipeable to TransformStreams and toStdout-like sinks in examples
Multiple concurrent consumers (2-5) receive full ordered token stream when within cache window
When network disconnect occurs, multiplexer auto-reconnects using SDK retry policy and replays cached prefix; consumers see a single continuous sequence separated by a boundary event
When consumer lags beyond cache window it receives a replay_gap event and stream continues without blocking producer
Unit tests cover buffer thresholds, cache eviction, resume boundary emission, and consumer detach/attach behavior
Integration test simulates token refresh mid-stream and verifies new handshake does not corrupt sequences for attached consumers

testing_plan: Unit tests: simulate a fake upstream that emits tokens at variable rates. Tests for multiple concurrent consumers, cache eviction, boundary events, and backpressure thresholds. Integration: run an end-to-end against staging runtime with induced TCP drop and auth refresh to validate resume logic. Performance: measure single-consumer median p99 latency before/after; goal is <5% regression. Add stress test that spins up 10 consumers for 1 minute to verify stable memory usage and correct eviction behavior.
